newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar weak on slow demand, limited activity.
newsitem.headline: India sugar weak on slow demand, limited activity.

text.p: Sugar prices were weak on the local market as consumer demand remained slow and prices slid in limited activity on Monday, dealers said.

In the ready delivery sugar S-30 slid by 10 rupees at 1,450/1,470 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 fell by 3 rupees at 1,475/1,505 rupees per quintal. Volume was poor as major players kept sidelines awaiting the announcement of the free sale quota for July by Indian government.
Meanwhile sugar mill delivery looked up on limited offerings by millers as they expect the government to announce a lower free sale quota, one broker said.

In the mill delivery, sugar S-30 rose by 10/15 rupees at 1,395/1,410 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 climbed up by 15 rupees at 1,420/1,440 rupees per quintal. The free sale quota for the current month is 800,000 tonnes and millers expect a quota of about 725,000/750,000 tonnes for July.
Overall market sentiment was quiet at the close of the session and physical activity remained at a low ebb as everybody in the market was keenly awaiting the quota announcement, a broker said.
